name: Buphagidae
description: Oxpeckers are a small family of passerine birds endemic to sub-Saharan Africa. They are well-known for their symbiotic relationship with large mammals, perching on them and feeding on ticks, blood, and parasites.

children.name: Buphagus
children.description: A genus of two species of tick-eating birds specialized for perching and foraging on large mammals.

children.name: Buphagus erythrorynchus
children.description: The red-billed oxpecker (Buphagus erythrorynchus) is a passerine bird in the oxpecker family, Buphagidae. It is native to the eastern savannah of sub-Saharan Africa, from the Central African Republic east to South Sudan and south to northern and eastern South Africa. It is more widespread than the yellow-billed oxpecker in Southern Africa, where their ranges overlap.

children.name: Buphagus africanus
children.description:
The yellow-billed oxpecker (Buphagus africanus) is a passerine bird in the family Buphagidae. It was previously placed in the starling and myna family, Sturnidae.
It is native to the savannah of Sub-Saharan Africa from Senegal east to Sudan. It is least common in the extreme east of its range where it overlaps with the red-billed oxpecker, despite always dominating that species when feeding.
